Cloth Scarf: Well now, come in out of the dark, traveler. Fire's warm and the stew's on. What'll it be?
布围巾: 哎呀，快从外头的黑暗里进来吧，旅人。炉火正暖，炖菜也在锅里咕嘟着呢。想来点什么？

Cloth Scarf: Tell me a tale of the forest.

Cloth Scarf: I found Ash. He's safe. See for yourself.

Cloth Scarf: Old-timers say this forest was old when the hills were young. Cross the water at the River Clearing and the trees start listening, and past the Green Glade, out in the Old Woods and the Primeval Woods beyond, they do more than listen. My gran swore she watched a great oak pull up its roots by moonlight and stride off between the groves. Folk call it the Wandering Oak, and nobody cuts timber where it's passed.
布围巾: 老一辈的人说，这片森林在群山还年轻的时候就已经苍老了。渡过河边空地的水流，树木便开始竖起耳朵倾听；再往前，穿过绿荫空地，进入老林子和更深处的远古林地，它们做的可就不只是倾听了。我祖母发誓说，她曾在月光下亲眼看见一棵大橡树拔起根须，在林间大步走开。村里人管它叫“漫游橡树”，它走过的地方，没人敢去砍伐。

Cloth Scarf: Go on.
布围巾: 接着说。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another night.
布围巾: 改天晚上再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Mind you, not everything walking those woods is timber. Shepherds up by the Moon Hills tell of the Humming Widow's lullaby drifting down after dusk, and away south in the Black Mire squats the Hag, she'll trade you wonders, sure, but her bargains cost dearer than salt. And on the coldest nights, when every wolf in the forest goes quiet at once? That's the Primeval Wolf passing through, and even the bears in the Bear Cave hold their breath.
布围巾: 不过啊，在那片林子里走动的，可不都是些木头精怪。月丘那边的牧羊人说，黄昏之后能听见“哼唱寡妇”的摇篮曲随风飘来；再往南边的黑泥沼里蹲着那个巫婆，她愿意跟你交换些稀奇东西，没错，可她的交易代价，比盐还贵。还有啊，最冷的那些夜里，要是整片森林里的狼突然一起安静下来——那就是远古狼在经过，就连熊穴里的熊都得屏住呼吸。

Cloth Scarf: Is any of it true?
布围巾: 这些都是真的吗？

Cloth Scarf: True enough that I keep salt on the sill and the fire lit. The forest gives: mushrooms, game, timber, and it takes. House rule: respect the groves, mind the mire, and be indoors by full dark.
布围巾: 真到我一直在窗台上放着盐、炉火从不熄灭的地步。森林给予：蘑菇、猎物、木材，它也索取。这屋子的规矩是：敬重树林，小心泥沼，天黑透之前一定要待在屋里。

Cloth Scarf: You've gone quiet. Something on your mind?
布围巾: 你突然不说话了，是在想什么吗？

Cloth Scarf: A fine tale. Thanks for the telling.
布围巾: 好故事，谢谢你讲给我听。

Cloth Scarf: Aye, it's our Ash. The inn's cat, gray as woodsmoke, eyes like embers, best mouser this side of the river. He slipped out three nights back and hasn't come home. A forager swears she saw him in the Foraging Forest, off the Village Path, prowling the ferns at dusk. Those trees are the Old Woods' little sister, no place for a house cat after dark.
布围巾: 唉，是我们家艾什。旅店的猫，毛色灰得像炊烟，眼睛亮得像炭火，是这条河这边最会抓老鼠的猫。三天前的晚上他溜出去，就再没回来。有个采集者信誓旦旦地说，在村间小径边上的觅食林里看见他，黄昏时分正在蕨丛里游荡。那片林子算是老林子的小妹妹，天黑之后可不是家猫该待的地方。

Cloth Scarf: I'll keep an eye out for him.
布围巾: 我会留意找他的。

Cloth Scarf: Cats find their own way home.
布围巾: 猫自己会找到回家的路的。

Cloth Scarf: Bless you. Dusk, mind, he never prowls by daylight. And he won't come to calling; hold out a bit of meat or fish and keep very still. Bring him home safe, or keep him fed, and he'll keep you.
布围巾: 太感谢你了。记住是黄昏时分，他白天从不出去游荡。叫他的名字是没用的，拿点肉或鱼出来，安安静静地等着就行。把他平安带回来，或者好好喂饱他，他也会一直陪着你的。

Cloth Scarf: I will.
布围巾: 我会的。

Cloth Scarf: Ash! Look at him, riding your pack like he owns it. Ha! He's chosen you, then; cats do the choosing, never us. Keep him fed and he'll keep the rats from your stores. Here, supper's on the house, and a little something for the road.
布围巾: 艾什！你看看他，趴在你的背包上，那副神气活现的样子，好像那包本来就是他的。哈！这么说，他选中你了；猫从来都是自己挑人，可轮不到我们挑。好好喂着他，他就会替你把老鼠赶出储藏室。来，今晚这顿饭我请，再给你带点路上吃的。

Cloth Scarf: He's in good hands. Thank you.
布围巾: 他在我这儿会过得很好的，谢谢你。

Cloth Scarf: Coldest winter in memory, that one. The wolves came down out of the high country thin and bold, right up to the fences, and old Tomas swore one of them looked him dead in the eye through his own window glass. Nobody much wanted watch duty after dark that season, and I don't blame them one bit. Traps came up empty three nights running, and torches only bought an hour's peace before the wolves crept back closer each time. It was the miller's wife who noticed something the rest of us had missed: the wolves never came within twenty paces of the smokehouse. Turned out the smell put their noses clean off the scent of anything worth hunting.

Cloth Scarf: She called the whole village into the square and had us hang strips of smoked hide and old fish bones along every fence post and gate, thick as bunting at a festival. Ripest the village ever smelled, I'll tell you, half the children held their noses just walking to bed, but by the third night not a single wolf set paw within a stone's throw of the walls. It held clean through to spring, and once the deer wandered back down from the hills the wolves lost interest in us entirely and went back to easier hunting. We still hang a strip of smoked hide over the north gate every winter to this day, more habit now than need, though old Tomas won't sleep a wink without it there. Funny thing, how a bit of good honest stink saved an entire village.

Cloth Scarf: Had a peddler come through one autumn, sharp dressed fellow, full of opinions about foraging he had no business holding. Insisted he knew his mushrooms better than any village forager, picked himself a nice fat cap out past the tree line, and ate it raw before anyone could stop him, wrong cap as it turned out, and wrong by quite a margin. Within the hour he was convinced the inn's rafters were speaking to him in verse, and not bad verse either, by his own account. He climbed up on this very table, arms out like a scarecrow, and announced to the whole common room that he'd been made an honorary badger, then spent a good twenty minutes bowing to the fireplace, calling it 'Your Grace.'

Cloth Scarf: He tried to trade his boots to the cat for what he called 'safe passage through the badger kingdom,' and the cat, being a sensible creature, wanted nothing to do with any of it. Somewhere in there he became convinced his own shadow was following him with intent to rob him, and spent a solid hour negotiating with it in the corner while my father just kept refilling water and moving the sharp objects out of reach. Come sunrise he woke up on the floor, boots still on his feet, utterly baffled why every soul in the inn was grinning at him over breakfast. Swore off foraging for himself forever after, and paid double for a proper forager's basket before he left, no questions asked. 布围巾: 他还想拿自己的靴子跟猫交换，说是换取“安全通过獾王国”，猫呢，是个明白事理的家伙，压根不想搭理这套。中间他还一度深信自己的影子在跟踪他，图谋不轨，硬是在角落里跟影子“谈判”了足足一个钟头，我父亲在旁边一个劲儿地添水，顺手把尖利的东西都收远了些。天亮的时候，他在地板上醒来，靴子还穿在脚上，完全搞不明白为什么吃早饭时满屋子人都冲他笑。从那以后他发誓再也不自己采蘑菇，临走前二话不说，花双倍的价钱买了个像样的采集篮子。直到今天，我还是会跟每个新来的人说：认不出蘑菇，吃之前先问一句，那个货郎的影子，欠着一份道歉呢，还没还清。

布围巾: “荣誉獾”，这称号我挺喜欢。

Cloth Scarf: Now this one my uncle swears is true, though he swears a great many things are true. Out on the river one summer evening, quiet water, not a ripple, when something took his line so hard it nearly dragged him clean off the bank, bending his rod into a shape no rod ought to bend into. He fought it for the better part of an hour, or so he tells it, and each retelling the hour grows a little longer. Said the fish surfaced once, just once, and looked him square in the eye with an expression he could only describe as disappointed in him personally. By his account it was the size of a rowboat, though the size seems to grow a bit with every winter that passes too.
布围巾: 这个故事，我叔叔发誓是真的，不过他发誓是真的事情多了去了。一个夏日的傍晚，他在河边钓鱼，水面平静得没有一丝涟漪，忽然有什么东西猛地咬住了他的钓线，差点把他整个人拽下河岸，鱼竿都弯成了不该有的形状。他跟那东西较量了大半个钟头——至少他自己是这么说的，而且每次重讲，这“大半个钟头”都会变得更长一点。他说那条鱼浮出水面过一次，就那么一次，直勾勾地盯着他的眼睛，那表情，他形容说只能叫“对他本人感到失望”。据他讲，那鱼有一艘小船那么大，不过这尺寸似乎也随着一年年冬天过去，越长越大了。

Cloth Scarf: Just as he had it near the bank, close enough to touch, the line snapped clean through, and the fish gave what he insists was a mocking little flick of its tail before it vanished back under. He came home soaked to the bone, empty handed, and utterly certain it was the finest fish that had ever lived in that river or any other, and nobody else was there to see a scale of it, of course, which he says is exactly the sort of detail a truly legendary fish arranges for itself. Half the village has started calling that stretch of river 'the old man's grief' just to needle him over it. He still fishes that same spot every summer, same rod even, waiting on what he calls a proper rematch. I've long since given up asking whether any of it happened the way he says, a good fish story doesn't need much truth in it to be worth the telling.
布围巾: 就在快要把鱼拉到岸边、伸手就能摸到的时候，钓线“啪”地一声断了，那鱼——他坚持说——甩了甩尾巴，那神气活像在嘲笑他，然后就沉回水底不见了。他浑身湿透地回到家，两手空空，却打心底认定那是那条河、乃至任何一条河里活过的最好的一条鱼，当然了，也没别人在场看见哪怕一片鱼鳞，他说这正是一条真正的传奇之鱼该安排的细节。村里有一半人开始把那段河叫“老头的伤心地”，就为了拿这事逗他。他每年夏天还是去那个老地方钓鱼，用的还是那根老鱼竿，等着他嘴里说的“堂堂正正的复仇之战”。我早就不问他讲的到底是不是真事了，一个好的钓鱼故事，本来就用不着多少真话才值得讲。

布围巾: 不管真假，这故事都值得一听。

布围巾: 我猜那条鱼自己也有个故事要讲。

Cloth Scarf: The miller's a proud man about that wheel of his, always has been, and one autumn a traveling grain merchant made the mistake of saying so within earshot. Merchant claimed his own family mill back wherever he hailed from could grind a sack of grain to fine flour faster than any wheel in this whole forest, and the miller near dropped his pipe hearing that. Wager was struck right there in the square before either of them thought better of it: a full cask of the inn's best cider against the merchant's finest travel cloak, first to grind a sack to proper baking flour wins outright. Half the village turned up to watch, more for the spectacle of two stubborn men than any real interest in flour, and the miller wouldn't let anyone near his wheel to help, said a fair contest needed a fair hand, his own.
布围巾: 磨坊主对他那座水车向来骄傲得很，一向如此。有一年秋天，一个跑单的粮商不识趣，当着他的面把这话说了出来。粮商说，他老家那座祖传的磨坊，磨一袋谷子出细面粉，比这片森林里的任何水车都快，磨坊主听完差点把烟斗都摔了。两人还没来得及多想，就当场在广场上打了赌：拿旅店最好的一桶苹果酒，赌粮商那件最好的旅行斗篷，谁先把一袋谷子磨成能烤面包的细面粉，谁就赢。半个村子的人都跑来看热闹，与其说是关心面粉，不如说是想看两个犟脾气的人怎么斗气。磨坊主谁都不让靠近他的水车帮忙，说公平的较量得靠一双公平的手，他自己的手。

Cloth Scarf: Merchant's method was all elbow grease and a hand quern he'd hauled along in his cart, fast at first but his arms gave out well before the sack did. Miller finished first by a good margin, flour fine as powder snow, and the merchant handed over that cloak with about as much grace as a man can manage while grumbling the whole time. They shared the cask of cider together that same night, thick as old friends by the time it was empty, and the merchant still stops through every harvest to needle the miller about that river's 'generosity.' Cloth Scarf: There's an old crossing further down the river, past where most folk care to wander, where they say a ferryman still waits for passengers who never quite arrive. My grandmother told it first, how on certain fog thick nights you can hear the creak of oarlocks out on the water with no boat in sight to match the sound; she never crossed there after dark again, not once in her whole life. Story goes he ferried travelers across for a fair coin his whole life, honest work, until one crossing in a storm the current took the boat and him with it, and he was never found. Some say he still keeps to his old post out of habit more than haunting, waiting on a fare that drowned along with him. Others say he's simply forgotten he's not needed anymore, and keeps rowing all the same.
布围巾: 河的下游有个老渡口，在大多数人都懒得去的地方，据说那儿还有个摆渡人，在等着永远不会到来的乘客。这故事最早是我祖母讲的，她说在雾特别浓的夜里，能听见水面上桨架“吱呀”作响，可根本看不见船的影子；打那以后，她这辈子再没在天黑后渡过那条河，一次都没有。故事是这么说的：他一辈子靠公道的价钱摆渡旅人，本本分分，直到有一次遇上暴风雨，水流把船和他一起卷走了，再没找到过。有人说他还守着老岗位，与其说是作祟，不如说是习惯，在等一个跟他一起淹死的乘客。也有人说，他只是忘了自己已经不被需要了，还在照样划着船。

布围巾: 有人见过他吗？

Cloth Scarf: A trapper I knew swore he saw a lantern bobbing low over the water one autumn night, right where the old landing used to stand before the river shifted its course. Called out to it, thinking it a traveler in trouble, and the light simply drifted off downstream without a word of answer, faster than any current should carry it. He didn't go back to that stretch of river again, not for trapping, not for anything, and truth be told I don't think anyone else rightly wants to either. Some tales are better left as tales, a light on the water, an old creak of oarlocks, nothing more than that so long as you keep your distance and mind your own crossing. All the same, if you ever find yourself down by that old landing after dark, I'd thank you to walk the long way round instead, just to be safe.
布围巾: 我认识的一个猎人发誓说，有一年秋夜，他看见一盏灯笼低低地在水面上晃悠，就在河流改道之前那个老渡口所在的位置。他冲着灯喊了一声，以为是遇上麻烦的旅人，结果那灯光一言不发地顺流飘走了，速度快得不像任何水流能带动的。从那以后他再没回过那段河，捕猎也好，别的事也罢，说实话我看谁都不太想去。有些故事最好就留作故事——水面上的一盏灯，桨架古老的“吱呀”声，仅此而已，只要你保持距离，管好自己的渡口就行。不过话说回来，你要是哪天天黑后正好路过那个老渡口，我劝你还是绕远路走，安全第一。

Cloth Scarf: Deliver Dried Wild Garlic

Cloth Scarf: Hand over the dried wild garlic the Inn Keeper asked for.
布围巾: 把旅店老板要的风干野蒜交给他。

Cloth Scarf: Would you look at that. The well's finished, deep and cold and true. My father would have liked seeing it done. Thank you for lending a hand.
布围巾: 你瞧瞧这个。井修好了，又深又凉，做得扎扎实实。我父亲要是能看到这一幕，一定会喜欢的。谢谢你搭了把手。

Cloth Scarf: It's good work. You should be proud.
布围巾: 干得漂亮，你该为此感到骄傲。

Cloth Scarf: Mostly the village's doing, really.
布围巾: 说到底，主要还是全村人的功劳。

Cloth Scarf: I hear the river's got a proper bridge across it now. Used to be you'd take your chances fording it, or not go at all. Makes this whole valley feel a little smaller, a little friendlier.
布围巾: 听说河上现在有座像样的桥了。以前过河全靠碰运气，要不就干脆不去。这下整个山谷都显得小了一圈，也更亲近了些。

Cloth Scarf: It's saved me a soaking more than once.
布围巾: 它可不止一次让我少挨了一身湿。

Cloth Scarf: Smaller and friendlier sounds right.
布围巾: “更小更亲近”，这话说得没错。

Cloth Scarf: Actually, glad you're here. We're closing up early tonight and walking out to the well together, whole village, for a proper toast. Won't be long. Care to come, or mind the hearth while we're gone?
布围巾: 说起来，正好你在这儿。今晚我们准备早点打烊，全村人一起走去水井那边，好好敬一杯。不会太久。你是想一起去，还是留下来帮我看着炉火？

Cloth Scarf: Wouldn't miss it.
布围巾: 这种场合我可不能错过。

Cloth Scarf: Go on. I'll keep an eye on things here.
布围巾: 你们去吧，这儿我来看着。

Cloth Scarf: "To the well," he says later, cup raised against the dark, "and to everyone fool enough to help dig it." The whole village laughs and drinks. By the time the fire's died down, he's already talking about what to build next.
布围巾: “敬这口井，”他后来举起杯子，对着夜色说道，“也敬所有傻乎乎跑来帮忙挖井的人。”全村人都笑着一饮而尽。等篝火渐渐熄灭时，他已经开始盘算接下来该建些什么了。

Cloth Scarf: A fine toast.
布围巾: 敬得好。

Cloth Scarf: Actually, I could use a hand with something. My dried wild garlic's run low and the stew's suffering for it. Bring me some and I'll make it worth your while.
布围巾: 说起来，我这儿正好有件事需要帮忙。风干野蒜快用完了，炖菜的味道都受了影响。给我带点来，我不会亏待你的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some.
布围巾: 我会给你带一些来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Still keeping an eye out for that dried wild garlic? No rush, but the stew's counting on you.
布围巾: 那风干野蒜的事，你还记着呢吧？不急，不过这炖菜可就指望你了。

Cloth Scarf: Working on it.
布围巾: 正在办呢。

Cloth Scarf: There you are. Sit, sit. I've been saving the good chair for whoever wandered in looking like they needed it most, and lately that's usually you.
布围巾: 你可来了，坐吧坐吧。这把好椅子我一直留着，给那个看起来最需要它的人坐，最近啊，那个人多半就是你。

Cloth Scarf: The Professor at the Academy?
布围巾: 学院里的那位教授吗？

Cloth Scarf: The Professor? Sharp as a tack and twice as dry. Comes down from the Academy some evenings for a bowl of stew and to grumble about students who don't read. Good company, once you get a few words out of him.
布围巾: 教授啊？脑子跟针一样尖，嘴皮子却干得能起皮。有些晚上他会从学院下来喝碗炖菜，顺便抱怨几句不肯读书的学生。跟他多聊几句之后，其实是个挺不错的伴儿。

Cloth Scarf: Good to know.
布围巾: 知道了。

Cloth Scarf: What do you make of the Inn Keeper down the way?
布围巾: 你觉得那边的旅店老板怎么样？

Cloth Scarf: The Inn Keeper? A good soul, and a better cook than any of us give credit for. I take my supper there most evenings, it's quieter than the lecture hall, and nobody asks me to grade anything.
布围巾: 旅店老板？心肠很好的一个人，厨艺也比我们这些人愿意承认的要好得多。我大半个晚上都在那儿吃饭，比讲堂安静多了，也没人缠着我批改作业。

Cloth Scarf: Good to know.
布围巾: 知道了。

Cloth Scarf: Got anything for trade?
布围巾: 有什么可以交易的吗？

Cloth Scarf: Where were your rounds today?
布围巾: 你今天都去了哪些地方？

Cloth Scarf: How am I doing as a student?
布围巾: 我作为学生表现如何？

Cloth Scarf: Test me, Professor.
布围巾: 考考我吧，教授。

Cloth Scarf: Any advice for a field scholar?
布围巾: 对一位田野学者有什么建议吗？

Cloth Scarf: How did you come to teach here?
布围巾: 你是怎么来这里任教的？

Cloth Scarf: The innkeeper's cat has taken to me.
布围巾: 旅店老板的猫喜欢上我了。

Cloth Scarf: The river bridge is finished.
布围巾: 河上的桥修好了。

Cloth Scarf: I had good teachers.
布围巾: 是因为我遇到了好老师。

Cloth Scarf: Stand still a moment. Six courses. Six! In all my years at this lectern nobody has taken every degree the Academy offers. Consider yourself, formally, our first Valedictorian. This purse is the endowment prize; I've been guarding it for someone worth handing it to.
布围巾: 稍站一会儿。六门课程。整整六门！我在这讲台前执教这么多年，从没有人修完过学院开设的每一个学位。请你正式接受这个称号——我们的第一位优等毕业生。这个钱袋是基金奖学金；我一直守着它，等一个配得上它的人出现。

Cloth Scarf: Thank you, Professor.
布围巾: 谢谢您，教授。

Cloth Scarf: One moment, before anything else. You've passed your first course. Do you know how few villagers ever finish one? Here, a small prize from the Academy's coffers. Put it toward your next enrollment, or don't; it's yours.
布围巾: 稍等一下，在别的事之前。你已经通过了你的第一门课程。你可知道，村里能修完一门课的人有多么稀少？来，这是学院金库里的一份小奖励。用它去报下一门课，或者不用，都随你，这是你的了。

Cloth Scarf: Come in, come in. Of everyone in this village, you're the only one who asks the right questions. Sit. What's on your mind?
布围巾: 进来吧，进来。在这个村子里，只有你会问出恰当的问题。坐下吧。你在想些什么？

Cloth Scarf: Ah, my favorite irregular student. I was hoping you'd stop by. What shall it be today?
布围巾: 啊，我最喜欢的这位非正规学生。我一直盼着你能来。今天想谈些什么？

Cloth Scarf: Spring again. The forest floor is a syllabus all its own, every seedling a footnote. What can I do for you?
布围巾: 又到了春天。林地本身就是一份教学大纲，每一株幼苗都是一条注脚。我能为你做些什么？

Cloth Scarf: A fine summer's day. I would lecture outdoors if the students wouldn't doze in the grass. What brings you?
布围巾: 好一个夏日。若不是学生们会在草地上打盹，我倒愿意到户外讲课。你此来所为何事？

Cloth Scarf: Autumn: harvest for farmers, examinations for scholars. Both reward preparation. Yes?
布围巾: 秋天：对农夫而言是收获，对学者而言是考试。二者都会回报有所准备的人。怎么了？

Cloth Scarf: Bitter out. A good season for study: the cold keeps the mind sharp and the students indoors. What do you need?
布围巾: 外面天寒地冻。倒是个宜于治学的季节：寒冷让头脑保持清醒，也让学生们乖乖待在室内。你需要什么？

Cloth Scarf: Noted, Professor.
布围巾: 明白了，教授。

Cloth Scarf: The path today: mostly gravel and gossip, but I picked up a few useful stones. Mind the ruts by the old fencepost if you head that way.
布围巾: 今日在小径上：大多是碎石和闲话，不过我捡到了几块有用的石头。你若朝那边去，留意老篱笆桩旁的车辙。

Cloth Scarf: The farmland. Good roots this time of year, if you know where the soil stays soft. The farmer thinks I'm mad, wading about the furrows with a satchel. He may be right.
布围巾: 农田。这个时节根茎长得不错，只要你知道哪里的土还软着。那位农夫觉得我疯了，提着个背包在田垄间跋涉。他大概说得没错。

Cloth Scarf: Just the village square, trading pleasantries and picking up oddments. One learns more at a market stall than in some lectures, though don't quote me to my students.
布围巾: 只是去了村广场，寒暄几句，顺手捡些零碎东西。有些道理，站在摊位前学到的，比在讲堂里学到的还多，不过这话你可别去转告我的学生。

Cloth Scarf: The Foraging Forest. Mind the nettles. Worth every sting, though; the understory was generous today. Half my satchel came from a single clearing.
布围巾: 觅食林。小心荨麻。不过每一下刺痛都是值得的；今天林下层收获颇丰。我半个背包的东西，都来自同一块空地。

Cloth Scarf: Frankly? You've yet to sit a single final. The lectern takes deposits of salt, nuggets, or coin, and I promise the hours pass faster than you fear. Come. Ignorance is curable.
布围巾: 坦白说？你还没参加过一次期末考试呢。讲台账户收盐、金属块或硬币作为存款，我向你保证，时间过得比你担心的要快得多。来吧。无知是可以治愈的。

Cloth Scarf: Coming along well. You've a degree to your name, more than most who drift through here. Keep at it; the Academy's best shelf is reserved for those who finish all six.
布围巾: 进展不错。你名下已经有一个学位了，比大多数在这里晃悠的人都强。继续努力吧；学院最好的那格书架，是留给修完全部六门课程的人的。

Cloth Scarf: You've finished everything I can teach. It's an odd feeling, being out of material. Visit anyway; colleagues are rarer than students.
布围巾: 你已经修完了我能教授的一切。没有更多东西可教，这种感觉挺奇怪的。不过还是常来吧；同僚可比学生稀罕得多。

Cloth Scarf: Advice? Carry twine. Half of field scholarship is tying bundles. The other half is writing things down before you forget where you found them. And never eat a mushroom you can't name twice.
布围巾: 建议？随身带上细绳。田野学问有一半是在打包捆扎，另一半是在忘记东西是从哪儿找到的之前把它写下来。还有，绝不要吃一种你连叫出两遍名字都做不到的蘑菇。

Cloth Scarf: Go on.
布围巾: 请继续。

Cloth Scarf: I taught in Duros, once: proper halls, proper stipends, proper politics. The politics won. A travelling merchant told me of a village raising an academy out of mud and stubbornness, and I found I preferred the stubbornness.
布围巾: 我曾在杜洛斯任教：正经的讲堂、正经的薪俸、正经的政治斗争。最后是政治斗争赢了。一位行商跟我说起，有个村子正靠着泥浆和固执建起一座学院，我发现，比起前者，我更偏爱后者。

Cloth Scarf: The first winter I lectured to three farmers and a goat. The goat left. The farmers stayed; one of them built the desk you've seen me at. You ask why I stay; that desk is why. Now, enough of an old man's history.
布围巾: 第一个冬天，我对着三个农夫和一只山羊讲课。山羊后来走了。农夫们留了下来；其中一个人打造了你见过我坐着的那张书桌。你问我为什么留下来，那张书桌就是原因。好了，一个老头的往事，说到这里也就够了。

Cloth Scarf: So YOU'RE the one Ash chose. That cat used to prowl my lecture hall as if he held the deed to it. Mind he doesn't sleep on your notes; he has a scholar's instinct for the exact page you need.
布围巾: 原来艾什选中的人是你啊。那只猫以前老在我讲堂里游荡，那副神气，好像这地方的地契在他手里似的。小心别让他睡在你的笔记上；他有种学者般的直觉，总能精准地压在你最需要的那一页上。

Cloth Scarf: The river bridge, finished at last! Do you know what a bridge is to a village like this? A thesis in timber, proof we intend to be more than a clearing with opinions. Enrollment will thank you within the season.
布围巾: 河上的桥，总算修好了！你可知道，对这样一个村子来说，一座桥意味着什么？那是一篇用木料写成的论文，证明我们不甘心只做一片有主见的空地。用不了一季，学院的报名人数就会因你而增长。

Cloth Scarf: Very well. A question from the entrance examination. A student returns from the forest fevered, with an angry wound. Which remedy do you reach for first?
布围巾: 很好。这是一道入学考试题。一名学生从森林归来，发着高烧，还带着一处红肿发炎的伤口。你会先取用哪种疗法？

Cloth Scarf: Raw spirit mushrooms, chewed slowly.
布围巾: 生的灵魂菇，慢慢咀嚼。

Cloth Scarf: A plantain poultice, cleaned and bound.
布围巾: 车前草敷剂，清创后包扎。

Cloth Scarf: A strong fireroot tea, piping hot.
布围巾: 一杯浓烈滚烫的火根茶。

Cloth Scarf: Precisely. Clean it, draw it, bind it; the poultice does the arguing. Full marks. The Academy awards small prizes for sound fundamentals; here.
布围巾: 正是如此。清创、拔毒、包扎；敷剂自会起效。满分。学院会为扎实的基本功颁发小奖励；给你。

Cloth Scarf: Mm. No. Your patient is now feverish AND disappointed. Review your herbals and ask me again. The examination allows retakes; the forest rarely does.
布围巾: 嗯，不对。你的病人现在不仅发着烧，还很失望。回去复习一下你的草药学，再来问我一次。考试允许重考，森林可不常给你这个机会。

Cloth Scarf: Specimen Request: 3 Nettle Leaves
布围巾: 标本请求：3片荨麻叶

Cloth Scarf: The Professor could use three nettle leaves for his herbarium presses. A scholar's errand, paid in metal.
布围巾: 教授需要三片荨麻叶用于他的植物标本压制。这是一件学者的差事，报酬以金属支付。

Cloth Scarf: Ah, perfect specimens, barely bruised! These go straight to the presses. Your pay, as promised. Keep an ear out; I'll have another errand within the week.
布围巾: 啊，完美的标本，几乎没有损伤！这些可以直接送去压制了。你的报酬，如约奉上。留意消息，一周之内我还会有新的差事。

Cloth Scarf: The Miller
布围巾: 磨坊主

Cloth Scarf: Moved into the Miller's Cottage a week after it was finished. Grinds the village's grain and keeps a pinch of every sack.
布围巾: 小屋建成一周后，磨坊主便搬了进来。他为全村磨制粮食，每袋都要抽取一小份作为报酬。

Cloth Scarf: Talk
布围巾: 交谈

Cloth Scarf: Chat
布围巾: 交谈

Cloth Scarf: Trade a little village gossip while the grindstones turn.
布围巾: 趁磨石转动的空当，和他聊几句村里的闲话。

Cloth Scarf: The Miller
布围巾: 磨坊主

Cloth Scarf: Ah, the builder! I wondered when you'd come knocking. The cottage suits me fine: stout walls, a dry floor, and room enough for the grindstones. The village has a miller again.
布围巾: 啊，是你，那个盖房子的！我还在想你什么时候会来敲门呢。这小屋合我心意：墙壁结实，地板干燥，磨石也有地方摆。村子总算又有磨坊主了。

Cloth Scarf: How's the milling trade?
布围巾: 磨坊的生意怎么样？

Cloth Scarf: How do you like the village?
布围巾: 你觉得这村子怎么样？

Cloth Scarf: Just passing through.
布围巾: 只是路过而已。

Cloth Scarf: Steady. The farm carts me their grain and I send back flour, and I keep a pinch of every sack, which is how a miller stays fed. Bring me a good harvest some autumn and you'll see the stones sing.
布围巾: 稳当。农田那边把粮食车过来，我磨成面粉送回去，每袋抽一小份，磨坊主就靠这个吃饭。哪年秋天你给我带来个好收成，就能听见磨石唱歌了。

Cloth Scarf: I'll leave you to it.
布围巾: 那我不打扰你了。

Cloth Scarf: It's young yet, but it has good bones: a well, honest neighbors, and now a roof of my own. A place worth grinding for. You built a piece of that, you know.
布围巾: 这地方还年轻，不过底子不错：一口井，几个实诚的邻居，如今还有了我自己的屋顶。是个值得为它磨粮食的地方。你知道吗，这里头也有你出的一份力。

Cloth Scarf: Glad to have you here.
布围巾: 很高兴你在这儿。

Cloth Scarf: Miller Move-In Day
布围巾: 磨坊主入住日

Cloth Scarf: Hidden tracker for the day the Miller moves into the finished cottage.
布围巾: 隐藏追踪器：记录磨坊主搬入建成小屋的那一天。

Cloth Scarf: The Weaver
布围巾: 织工

Cloth Scarf: Moved into the Weaver's Cottage a week after it was finished. Keeps a loom by the window and the village in cloth.
布围巾: 小屋建成一周后，织工便搬了进来。她在窗边支起一台织机，为全村提供布料。

Cloth Scarf: Talk
布围巾: 交谈

Cloth Scarf: Chat
布围巾: 交谈

Cloth Scarf: Pass the time to the clack of the loom and a bit of easy talk.
布围巾: 伴着织机咔嗒作响的节奏，和她轻松地聊聊天，消磨时光。

Cloth Scarf: The Weaver
布围巾: 织工

Cloth Scarf: Oh! Come in out of the wind. You're the one who raised this cottage, aren't you? I've set the loom up by the window, best light in the whole village, if you ask me.
布围巾: 哦！快进来避避风吧。你就是盖起这座小屋的人，对吧？我把织机摆在了窗边，要我说，这可是全村光线最好的地方。

Cloth Scarf: What are you weaving?
布围巾: 你在织什么？

Cloth Scarf: Settling in all right?
布围巾: 安顿得还顺利吗？

Cloth Scarf: I'll let you get back to it.
布围巾: 那我不打扰你干活了。

Cloth Scarf: Cloth for whoever needs it: plain and warm for winter, finer stuff when traders come through. A village that makes its own cloth never goes cold, that's what my mother always said.
布围巾: 谁需要布料我就织给谁：冬天要的是朴素保暖的，商人路过时就织些精细点的。一个能自己织布的村子，永远不会挨冻——我母亲一直这么说。

Cloth Scarf: Lovely work.
布围巾: 织得真好。

Cloth Scarf: Better than all right. Well water for washing wool, neighbors who wave hello, and a door that latches against the wind. I've thread enough to stay a long while; thank you for the roof, truly.
布围巾: 岂止是顺利。井水能洗羊毛，邻居见面都会打招呼，门也能挡住风。我这儿线够我用上好一阵子的了；谢谢你给我这个屋顶，真心的。

Cloth Scarf: Happy to have you in the village.
布围巾: 很高兴你能加入这个村子。

Cloth Scarf: Weaver Move-In Day
布围巾: 织工入住日

Cloth Scarf: Hidden tracker for the day the Weaver moves into the finished cottage.
布围巾: 隐藏追踪器：记录织工搬入建成小屋的那一天。

Cloth Scarf: A stout hardwood club carved from a tree trunk. Crude, but dependable blunt power.
布围巾: 一根用树干雕成的粗壮硬木棍棒，虽然简陋，但钝击威力可靠。

Cloth Scarf: Durability

布围巾: 把棍棒削成一根可用的长木棍。

Cloth Scarf: A simple cloth face covering tied behind the head. Keeps the wind and the worst of the dust off your face.
布围巾: 一块系在脑后的简易布制面罩，能挡住风沙，减轻脸部所受的尘土侵扰。

布围巾: 撕开口罩，回收布料。

Cloth Scarf: Sew a simple face covering from a piece of cloth and twine.
布围巾: 用一块布和麻绳缝制一件简易的面部遮挡物。

Cloth Scarf: The Weaver and Apothecary's masks for powder work
布围巾: 织工与药剂师为粉尘作业准备的口罩

布围巾: 保暖长裤

Cloth Scarf: Snug cloth leggings worn under trousers. An extra layer between you and the cold, with a little padding besides.
布围巾: 一条贴身的布制内裤，穿在长裤内侧。为你抵御寒冷多加一层保护，还带有些许保暖填充。

布围巾: 状况

布围巾: 长内裤已经磨穿。

布围巾: 釉面陶盘

布围巾: 在陶盘上涂抹灰釉并二次烧制，制成坚固光亮的餐具。

Cloth Scarf: Bring the Inn Keeper dried foragables for the winter pantry
布围巾: 为旅店老板的冬季储藏带来风干的野外食材

Cloth Scarf: Hunting Stand Kit
布围巾: 猎人瞭望台套件

Cloth Scarf: Planks, poles, and lashings bundled for raising an elevated hunting stand against a tree.
布围巾: 一捆木板、木杆和绑索，用于在树旁搭建一座高台猎人瞭望台。

布围巾: 搭建

布围巾: 把平台绑在此处一棵结实的树上。

布围巾: 猎人瞭望台

布围巾: 一座绑在树上的简易高台。离地而立能让掠食者更难发现你。

布围巾: 黄昏之后，艾什悄悄溜了出去，紧追着灌木丛里某种气味的踪迹。

Cloth Scarf: Ash, On the Hunt
布围巾: 出猎的艾什

Cloth Scarf: Ash didn't come home. He's gone to Hunter's Crossing — head there to find him. Once you do he'll have a boar cornered in the thicket.
布围巾: 艾什没有回家。它去了猎人岔口——前往那里寻找它。找到它时，它已经把一头野猪逼到了灌木丛中。

Cloth Scarf: Corner the Boar
布围巾: 逼退野猪

Cloth Scarf: Ash has the boar pinned in the thicket. Move in together and force the fight.
布围巾: 艾什已经把野猪逼进了灌木丛。一起上前，逼它决一死战。

Cloth Scarf: Ash's Trail
布围巾: 艾什的踪迹

Cloth Scarf: A tuft of grey fur and a scuff of paw prints in the mud. Ash slipped out after dark — the tracks lead toward Hunter's Crossing.
布围巾: 一撮灰色的毛发和泥地上一串模糊的爪印。艾什在天黑后溜了出去——足迹指向猎人岔口。

Cloth Scarf: Apothecary's Cabin

Cloth Scarf: Got a story for me?
布围巾: 有什么故事要讲给我听吗？

Cloth Scarf: Anything you need a hand with?
布围巾: 有什么需要帮忙的吗？

Cloth Scarf: Actually, since you're asking. My own store's run thin and the farm's grain hasn't come round yet this week. Bring me a wheat grain and I'll owe you one. Nothing fancy, just don't want the stones sitting idle.
布围巾: 说起来，你既然问了。我自己的存货快见底了，这周农田那边的粮食还没送来。给我带点小麦谷粒，我欠你一份人情。不用多讲究，就是不想让磨石闲着。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some.
布围巾: 我会给你带一些来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: There we are. Stones'll sing again by morning. I won't forget this, you're the sort of neighbor this village needed, and didn't know it yet.
布围巾: 这就对了。明早磨石就又能唱歌了。这份情我记下了，你正是这村子需要的那种邻居，只是它自己还不知道罢了。

Cloth Scarf: Glad to help.
布围巾: 很高兴能帮上忙。

Cloth Scarf: A story? Ha. All right, since you built me the roof. Years back, before I ever came here, I milled in a town three valleys over. There was another miller across the river, proud man, and one harvest we made a wager: whoever ground a full cart of grain fastest by sundown kept the other's best grindstone.
布围巾: 故事？哈。行吧，看在你给我盖了屋顶的份上。多年以前，我还没来这儿之前，是在三座山谷之外的一个镇子上磨粮食的。河对岸有另一个磨坊主，是个骄傲的人，有一年收获季我们打了个赌：日落之前谁先磨完一整车谷子，谁就赢走对方最好的一块磨石。

Cloth Scarf: And? Who won?
布围巾: 然后呢？谁赢了？

Cloth Scarf: I did, by two full sacks. But here's the thing about a wheel wager: it isn't the arms that win it, it's the water. I'd spent the whole week before quietly clearing the leaves and silt out of my own millrace so the wheel ran free, while his was choking half-shut and he never thought to look.
布围巾: 我赢了，多磨了整整两袋。不过水车这种赌局有个门道：赢的靠的不是胳膊，是水。我提前一整个星期，悄悄把自己水渠里的落叶和淤泥清干净了，让水车转得畅快，而他那边的渠道堵了大半，他压根没想过去看看。

Cloth Scarf: Did you play fair?
布围巾: 你这算公平吗？

Cloth Scarf: Fair? I kept my own house in order and he didn't, that's all. Nothing in the wager said a word about whose race ran cleaner. Still, I'll grant you it wasn't the whole of it, and I've never quite told it straight to anyone until now.
布围巾: 公平？我把自己的事打理好了，他没有，仅此而已。赌约里可没提谁的水渠更干净这回事。不过我承认，这也不是全部真相，这话我到今天都没跟人说明白过。

Cloth Scarf: So you admit it.
布围巾: 这么说你承认了。

Cloth Scarf: Your secret's safe with me.
布围巾: 你的秘密我会保密的。

Cloth Scarf: He took it in good humor in the end, once his temper cooled. Told me a miller who watches his water deserves the wheel, and gave me the grindstone without another word. I've cleared my race every week since, out of respect for him as much as habit. Just don't go repeating the water part around the village, eh?
布围巾: 他后来气消了，倒也想得开。说一个懂得照看自己水渠的磨坊主，配得上这块磨石，二话不说就把石头给了我。从那以后我每周都清理水渠，一半是习惯，一半也是对他的敬意。你可别把这水渠的事在村里传出去啊？

Cloth Scarf: Wouldn't dream of it.
布围巾: 想都不会想。

Cloth Scarf: Got a story for me?
布围巾: 有什么故事要讲给我听吗？

Cloth Scarf: Anything you need a hand with?
布围巾: 有什么需要帮忙的吗？

Cloth Scarf: If you're passing the farm rows, I've a pattern I've been dying to try, but it wants more flax than my own plot gives up in a season. Bring me a good bundle of dried flax stems and I'll show you something worth the wait.
布围巾: 你要是路过农田那一带，我这儿有个一直想试试的花样，可它要的亚麻，比我自己那块地一季能长出来的还多。给我带一捆好好晒干的亚麻茎来，我让你看看什么叫值得等待。

Cloth Scarf: I'll gather some for you.
布围巾: 我会去给你收集一些的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Oh, this'll do nicely. Here, I sketched a wall hanging out ages ago and never had the flax to spare for a first try. The pattern's yours now, same as the idea was. Loom's always warm if you want to see it made.
布围巾: 哦，这个正合适。给，我很久以前就画好了一幅壁挂的图样，一直没有多余的亚麻能试上第一次。现在这花样是你的了，就像这个点子本来也是你我共有的。你要是想看它织出来是什么样子，织机随时都是热乎的。

Cloth Scarf: Thank you, I'll treasure it.
布围巾: 谢谢你，我会好好珍惜的。

Cloth Scarf: A story. Let me think. My mother wove before me, and hers before her. The last winter she was well, she was spinning a spindle of nettle-fiber thread by the fire, thin as a hair and twice as stubborn. She said nettle punishes a lazy hand but never a patient one.
布围巾: 一个故事啊，让我想想。我母亲在我之前织布，她的母亲又在她之前织布。她身体还好的最后一个冬天，坐在炉火边纺一锭荨麻纤维线，细得像头发丝，倔得也是双倍。她说荨麻专挑懒手的麻烦，从不为难有耐心的人。

Cloth Scarf: What happened to it?
布围巾: 后来那锭线怎么样了？

Cloth Scarf: She never finished it. She got too weak to hold the spindle steady, and it sat on the shelf half-spun through the whole of that last spring. I couldn't bring myself to touch it. It felt like finishing it would mean she was really gone.
布围巾: 她没能织完。她后来虚弱得连纺锤都握不稳了，那锭线就那么半纺着，在架子上放了整整一个春天。我一直下不了手去碰它。总觉得，把它织完，就等于承认她真的不在了。

Cloth Scarf: Did you ever pick it up?
布围巾: 你后来接着做了吗？

Cloth Scarf: A full year later, on the first cold night, I finally sat down and spun the rest of it. My hands remembered hers, somehow. The thread came out even, no knots, no breaks, the whole length of it. I still don't know how, patient hand or not. I keep telling myself I made it. Truthfully I think we made it together.
布围巾: 整整一年后，在第一个寒冷的夜里，我终于坐下来把剩下的纺完了。不知怎么的，我的手竟然记得她的手法。那线纺得均匀，没有一个结，没有一处断，整整一根都是。到现在我也说不清是怎么做到的，是不是耐心的手也说不准。我总跟自己说，是我织出来的。可说实话，我觉得是我们俩一起织成的。

Cloth Scarf: What did you do with the thread?
布围巾: 那根线你后来用来做什么了？

Cloth Scarf: I wove it into the hem of the shawl I wear every winter, this one, here. You'd never pick it out from the rest, and that's the point. She's a single thread running through the whole of it, holding, not breaking. So when I tell you a good thread is worth waiting a year for, you understand I mean it more than one way.
布围巾: 我把它织进了我每年冬天都披的这条披肩的下摆里，就是这条，你看。你根本认不出它和别的线有什么不同，这正是它的意义所在。她就是贯穿整条披肩的那一根线，撑着，从不断裂。所以我跟你说一根好线值得等上一年，你该明白，我这话不止一层意思。

Cloth Scarf: That's the finest thing I've heard in a long while.
布围巾: 这是我很久以来听过最动人的事了。

Cloth Scarf: Anything else you're short on?
布围巾: 还缺什么别的东西吗？

Cloth Scarf: Since you're forever in those woods anyway, there are three things I've never enough of on hand: billberries, springberries, and spirit mushrooms, all fresh, mind, not dried. Bring me all three together and I'll finally have what I need for something stronger than what I sell.
布围巾: 反正你总在那片林子里跑，我手头总是缺三样东西：越橘、春莓和灵魂菇，记住，都要新鲜的，不是风干的。把这三样一起给我带来，我就总算能凑齐做点比我平时卖的东西更强效的材料了。

Cloth Scarf: I'll keep an eye out for all three.
布围巾: 我会留意这三样东西的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll see what I can do.
布围巾: 我看看能做些什么。

Cloth Scarf: All three, and none of them bruised. You've got a forager's hands, whether you know it or not. Give me a day or so and I'll have something worth more than a tea for it. Here, the recipe's yours too; you've earned the knowing of it.
布围巾: 三样都齐了，一个都没压坏。你这双手天生就是采集的料，不管你自己知不知道。给我一天左右的时间，我会做出比一杯茶更值钱的东西。来，这个方子也给你，你配得上知道它。

Cloth Scarf: Happy to forage for you.
布围巾: 很乐意为你去采集。

Cloth Scarf: Need anything pressed for your herbarium?
布围巾: 你的标本室还需要压制什么标本吗？

Cloth Scarf: As it happens, I've a standing request on the board for nettle leaves, three fresh ones, whenever you've a moment in the forest. Small thing, but my herbarium thanks you all the same.
布围巾: 说来正好，告示板上我留了个长期的请求——三片新鲜荨麻叶，等你有空进森林的时候顺手采一下。小事一桩，不过我的标本室仍会因此感激你。

Cloth Scarf: I'll keep an eye out.
布围巾: 我会留意的。

Cloth Scarf: You know, this inn's always had exactly one cat. Never two, never none for long, just the one. Ash isn't the first. Before him there was an old three-legged tom named Soot, black as a cold hearth, and he picked my father the very same way Ash picked you: walked in unbidden one evening and simply decided he lived here.
布围巾: 你知道吗，这家旅店向来只养一只猫。从来不是两只，也不会长时间一只都没有，就是一只。艾什不是第一只。在他之前有只三条腿的老公猫，叫“煤灰”，黑得像熄灭的炉膛，他当年选中我父亲的方式，跟艾什选中你一模一样：一天傍晚不请自来，径直走进屋子，就决定要住下了。

Cloth Scarf: What became of Soot?
布围巾: “煤灰”后来怎么样了？

Cloth Scarf: One hard winter he wandered off into the Old Woods and never came back. We looked, I'll tell you, we looked for weeks. And then for two full years, not a single cat came near the place. Not a stray, not a barn kitten, nothing. It was as if the inn itself was in mourning and wouldn't take another.
布围巾: 一个艰难的冬天，他走进老林子，再也没回来。我们找过，真的找过，找了好几个星期。之后整整两年，没有一只猫靠近过这地方。流浪猫没有，谷仓里的小猫也没有，什么都没有。就好像这家旅店自己在守丧，不肯再接纳别的猫。

Cloth Scarf: And then Ash turned up?
布围巾: 后来艾什就出现了？

Cloth Scarf: The very week the well was finished, out he strolled from nowhere, this scruffy young thing, and made himself at home on the warm hearthstone like he'd always owned it. I've chosen to believe, half in jest and half not, that a place only earns a cat again once it's proven it deserves one. And you helped prove it.
布围巾: 就在水井修好的那个星期，他不知从哪儿溜达出来，一只毛茸茸的小家伙，径直趴在温暖的炉石上，那副样子，好像这地方一直就是他的。我愿意相信——半开玩笑半认真地——一个地方只有证明自己配得上，才能再次拥有一只猫。而你，正是帮着证明了这一点的人。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe he was just waiting for the right place to be worth it.
布围巾: 也许他只是在等一个真正值得的地方。

布围巾: 把新鲜灵魂菇交给药剂师。她小心翼翼地捧着，嘴里念叨着这东西没坏地送来是多么难得。

Cloth Scarf: Well now, come in, come in. A new face in the valley is rarer than a dry spring. Sit; the fire doesn't charge. I keep this inn, and if you mean to last in these woods, you and I ought to get acquainted first.
布围巾: 哎呀，快进来，快进来。这山谷里出现张新面孔，比干旱的春天还稀罕。坐吧，炉火不收钱。这家旅店是我在打理，你要是打算在这片林子里长久待下去，咱俩得先认识认识。

Cloth Scarf: How do things work around here?
布围巾: 这地方是怎么运作的？

Cloth Scarf: Just warming my hands for now.
布围巾: 暂时只是来暖暖手。

Cloth Scarf: Simple enough. Minted coin is scarce out here; what the village trusts is salt and metal. Salt, nuggets, coins: all of it spends. Leave a deposit with me and I'll keep you an account, meals and a warm bed drawn against it at fair rates. The Academy across the way runs the same: the Professor draws tuition from a lectern account for his courses. Earn, deposit, spend: that's the whole economy.
布围巾: 说来简单。这地方铸币稀罕，村里信得过的是盐和金属。盐、金属块、硬币——都能花。把东西存到我这儿，我给你开个账户，饭菜和床铺都能按公道的价钱从里头扣。对面的学院也是一样的规矩：教授的课业学费也是从讲台账户里扣的。挣、存、花，整套经济就是这么回事。

Cloth Scarf: Anything around here I could help with?
布围巾: 这附近有什么我能帮上忙的吗？

Cloth Scarf: I'll think it over.
布围巾: 我会考虑一下的。

Cloth Scarf: Now that you ask, this village dreams bigger than its hands. A proper cottage for a miller: there's a man who'd grind grain for the whole valley if he had a roof over his stones. Another for a weaver, so we stop hauling every bolt of cloth in by cart. And a Village Hall, so the place finally has a heart to gather in. Help raise them, and you'll find this village doesn't forget its friends.
布围巾: 你既然问了，这村子的梦想啊，比手头能做的事大得多。得给磨坊主盖一座像样的小屋——那人只要石磨上有片屋顶，愿意给全山谷的人磨粮食。还得给织工也盖一座，免得我们每匹布都得靠马车运进来。再有就是村公所，让这地方总算有个大伙儿能聚在一起的心脏。帮着把这些建起来，你会发现这村子不会忘记自己的朋友。

Cloth Scarf: Count me in.
布围巾: 算我一个。

Cloth Scarf: Ha! I knew I liked you. The plans are yours to study whenever you're ready, no rush; the village has waited this long. Ask around, lend a hand where you can, and watch this valley wake up. My door's always open: a meal, a bed, or a look through the pantry.
布围巾: 哈！我就知道我看你顺眼。图纸随时给你看，不急，这村子都等了这么久了，也不差这一会儿。四处问问，能搭把手就搭一把，看着这山谷慢慢苏醒过来。我这门一直开着：一顿饭、一张床，或者到储藏柜里看看都行。

Cloth Scarf: (Shake his hand)
布围巾: （与他握手）

Cloth Scarf: The short of it: salt, nuggets, and coins are what spend here. Leave a deposit with me and your meals and bed draw against it; the Professor's lectern takes tuition the same way. And the projects: the Miller's Cottage, the Weaver's Cottage, and the Village Hall. The plans are in your journal; the hope is all ours.
布围巾: 简单说：盐、金属块和硬币，在这儿都能花。把东西存到我这儿，饭菜和床铺就从里头扣；教授的讲台收学费也是一个道理。至于那些建设项目：磨坊主的小屋、织工的小屋，还有村公所。图纸都在你的日志里，盼头是我们大伙儿共同的。

Cloth Scarf: Thanks for the refresher.
布围巾: 谢谢你再说一遍。

Cloth Scarf: Remind me how the village works.
布围巾: 再跟我说说这村子是怎么运作的。

Cloth Scarf: Hm? Ah, forgive me, I don't lecture strangers. In this valley introductions come first: present yourself to the Keeper at the Inn, let him show you how the village works. Once you're acquainted, my door, and my syllabus, will be open to you.
布围巾: 嗯？啊，恕我直言，我不给陌生人授课。在这山谷里，介绍认识是头一件事：先去旅店拜见店主，让他给你讲讲这村子是怎么运作的。等彼此熟识之后，我的门，还有我的课程表，随时向你敞开。

Cloth Scarf: I'll go and introduce myself.
布围巾: 我这就去自我介绍一下。

Save the two of us the formal introductions, then: this inn is yours to use, meals and a bed both, the village's projects are open for the helping, and the Academy across the way will take you as a student any day you like. Ask around and settle in.
布围巾: 你可来了！我敢说你还没走进这门，我就好像已经认识你了，风声传得快，我早就把你当自己人了。那咱俩就省了那套正式的介绍：这家旅店随你用，饭菜和床铺都算你的，村里的建设项目随时欢迎你帮忙，对面的学院你想什么时候去当学生都行。到处问问，安顿下来吧。

Cloth Scarf: Good to finally meet you properly.
布围巾: 总算正式认识你了，太好了。

布围巾: 隐藏追踪器：0=村庄旅店特质的一次性欢迎台词尚未播放，1=已播放（仅可触发一次）。

Cloth Scarf: I'll see what she can spare.
布围巾: 我去看看她能匀出些什么。

Cloth Scarf: Grinding powders kicks up more dust than you'd think, gets in the eyes, the nose, everywhere. If the Weaver can spare a length of cloth, I could sew myself a proper mask instead of tying a rag over my face like some bandit.
布围巾: 磨粉末扬起的灰尘，比你想的要多，眼睛里、鼻子里，哪儿都是。织工要是能匀出一段布，我就能给自己缝一个像样的口罩，不用再拿块破布蒙脸，跟个强盗似的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll pass that along.
布围巾: 我会带话给她的。

Cloth Scarf: Good weave, tight enough to keep the worst of the dust out. Tell the Weaver her cloth's finally doing honest work for someone other than herself. Here, the pattern's yours, in case you've a dusty errand of your own someday.
布围巾: 织得真好，密实得能挡住大部分灰尘。跟织工说一声，她的布终于替她自己以外的人干了件实在活。给，这花样也给你，说不定哪天你自己也要干灰尘满天的活儿呢。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you both.
布围巾: 我会把两样都带给你的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll see what I can find.
布围巾: 我看看能找到些什么。

Cloth Scarf: Since you're asking, I could use charcoal and a good handful of dried heather flowers. Grind them right and you get a pigment worth more than the sum of its parts, dyes, paints, all sorts of uses.
布围巾: 你既然问了，我正好需要木炭和一大把风干的石楠花。磨对了法子，能磨出一种颜料，比原材料本身值钱得多，染色、上漆，各种用途都有。

Cloth Scarf: Glad to help.
布围巾: 很高兴能帮上忙。

Cloth Scarf: Good char, good flowers, no waste in either. Grind them together and you've got yourself a proper pigment. Take the trick, I've no use hoarding it.
布围巾: 木炭好，花也好，两样都没浪费。一起磨碎，你就有了一份像样的颜料。这个诀窍你拿去吧，我留着也没用。

Cloth Scarf: Could the Weaver help with your dust problem?
布围巾: 织工能帮你解决灰尘的问题吗？

Cloth Scarf: What about powders and dyes?
布围巾: 粉末和染料的事怎么样了？

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a piece of charcoal for the Apothecary's powder work. She sets it aside with the rest of her grinding stock.
布围巾: 把一块木炭交给药剂师，用于她的制粉工作。她把它和其他待磨的存货放在一起。

Cloth Scarf: Give Charcoal
布围巾: 给予木炭

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a length of cloth for a dust mask. She holds it up to her face to check the fit.
布围巾: 把一段布交给她，用来做防尘口罩。她把布举到脸上比了比大小。

Cloth Scarf: Give Cloth
布围巾: 给予布料

Cloth Scarf: Hand over dried heather flowers for the Apothecary's powder work. She crumbles a petal between her fingers, testing the dryness.
布围巾: 把风干的石楠花交给药剂师，用于她的制粉工作。她用手指捻碎一片花瓣，试试干燥程度。

布围巾: 给予风干石楠花

Cloth Scarf: I'll see what he's got milled.

Cloth Scarf: I've a mind to set a proper baking day, but I'm short on milled flour. The Miller's got a mill sitting idle half the week, if you'd bring me some of what he grinds, wheat or rye, either does.
布围巾: 我一直想定个正经的烤面包日，可手头的面粉不够。磨坊主的磨坊一周有大半时间都闲着，你要是能把他磨的粮食给我带点来，小麦也好，黑麦也好，都成。

Cloth Scarf: I'll pass that along.
布围巾: 我会带话给他的。

Cloth Scarf: Good fine grind, the Miller knows his stones. Baking day's on for certain now. Tell him the whole Inn will smell like bread by supper, that ought to please him. Here, a plate pattern for the trouble, freshly painted to match the occasion.
布围巾: 磨得真细，磨坊主懂他那几块磨石。烤面包日这下是定下来了。跟他说，晚饭时分整家旅店都会飘着面包香，这话他听了肯定高兴。来，这个盘子花样给你，作为谢礼，特意配着这个场合新画的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll see what she's got.
布围巾: 我去看看她有什么。

Cloth Scarf: Between you and me, some of my regulars overdo it on brew night and I'm tired of hearing about it the morning after. The Apothecary's herb paste settles a stomach better than anything I've tried. Bring me some and I'll keep it behind the bar.
布围巾: 跟你说句悄悄话，酿酒之夜有几个常客总是喝过头，第二天早上我都听腻了他们抱怨。药剂师的草药膏比我试过的任何东西都更能安抚肠胃。给我带点来，我就放在柜台后面备着。

Cloth Scarf: I'll pass that along.
布围巾: 我会带话给她的。

Cloth Scarf: That'll settle a few stomachs come morning. Tell the Apothecary the whole common room owes her a favor she'll never collect on. Here, a burner pattern for the trouble, might as well have something nice for the bar too.
布围巾: 这下第二天早上能安抚不少人的肠胃了。跟药剂师说一声，满屋子的人都欠她一份还不清的人情。来，这个香炉花样给你，作为谢礼，柜台这边也该有点像样的东西了。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you a stew.
布围巾: 我会给你带炖菜来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Truth told, the pot's been lonely lately, same broth every night wears thin. Bring me a hot cooked stew and I'll dish it up proper, might even earn you a keepsake for the trouble.
布围巾: 说实话，锅子最近挺冷清的，天天都是那锅老汤，味道都淡了。给我带一锅热腾腾的炖菜来，我会好好盛给大家吃，说不定还能给你留个纪念品当谢礼。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some ale.
布围巾: 我会给你带麦酒来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Brew night's coming and my own stock's run dry. Bring me a beer or ale and I'll make sure it's poured right, on the house even, once or twice.
布围巾: 酿酒之夜快到了，我自己的存货都见底了。给我带点啤酒或者麦酒来，我保证给你倒得规规矩矩，说不定还能请你喝一两回。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you a wine.
布围巾: 我会给你带葡萄酒来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: For the top shelf, mind, not the common stock, I'd like a wine or a second brew, something worth setting aside for a good occasion. Bring me one and I'll make it worth your while.
布围巾: 记住，是要放在最好的那层架子上，不是普通存货，我想要一瓶葡萄酒，或者一份上等的酿酒，值得留着等好日子用的那种。给我带一份来，我不会亏待你的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some dried foragables.
布围巾: 我会给你带些风干的采集物来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Winter's the hardest stretch for a pantry. Bring me some dried mushrooms or dried berries, whatever you've got put by, and I'll square us up proper come the thaw.
布围巾: 冬天对储藏柜来说是最难熬的一段日子。给我带点风干蘑菇或者风干浆果，不管你存了什么都行，等雪化了我一定好好谢你。

Cloth Scarf: Glad the pot's happy again.
布围巾: 很高兴这锅子又热闹起来了。

Cloth Scarf: Now that's a proper stew, thick and hearty, the kind that sticks to a traveler's ribs on a cold night. The whole common room will smell of it by supper, and I expect a crowd once word gets around. Here, a painted bowl to serve it in, real color to it instead of plain clay, the least the pot deserves after being neglected so long.
布围巾: 这才叫像样的炖菜，浓稠扎实，寒夜里能给旅人暖到骨头里的那种。晚饭时分整个大堂都会飘着这味道，消息一传开，我看会有不少人来。来，这个彩绘碗给你盛菜用，比素面的陶碗有色彩多了，这也是那口被冷落了这么久的锅，最起码该得的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll drink to that.
布围巾: 这个我得喝一杯庆祝。

Cloth Scarf: Brew night's saved, and just in time too, half the regulars were already grumbling about a dry bar before you walked in. Here's a painted cup to pour it in, better than the chipped ones we've been making do with since my father's day. Cheers, when you've a moment to sit, you've more than earned the first pour.
布围巾: 酿酒之夜有救了，来得也是时候，你进门之前，半数常客都已经在抱怨吧台没酒了。这个彩绘杯子给你，用来倒酒，比我们从我父亲那辈就将就着用的那些缺口杯子强多了。干杯，等你有空坐下来，第一杯酒该敬你，你受得起。

Cloth Scarf: Save me a glass when it does.
布围巾: 到时候给我留一杯。

Cloth Scarf: Now that's a top-shelf pour if I ever saw one, the kind I'll be saving for someone's wedding toast or the day the Village Hall finally got its roof. Here's a painted vase to keep it in until the right occasion comes along, and around here, one always does sooner or later. You've got a good eye for quality, I'll say that for you.
布围巾: 这可真是我见过最上等的一份，我打算留着，等谁家办婚礼敬酒，或者村公所终于盖上屋顶那天再拿出来。这个彩绘花瓶给你，用来存放它，等到合适的场合，这地方迟早会有的。你这眼光挑东西是真准，这话我得说给你听。

Cloth Scarf: Here's hoping for plenty more.
布围巾: 希望以后还能有更多。

Cloth Scarf: Now the pantry's set for the worst of it, shelves packed tight enough that I won't be lying awake fretting over the deep frost this year. Here, a glazed plate, tougher than the plain clay, fired twice over so it won't crack the first time someone sets it down too hard. Ought to last through however many winters this Inn has left in it, and I mean to see quite a few more of them yet.
布围巾: 这下储藏柜准备好过最难熬的时候了，架子堆得满满当当，今年严寒我再也不用躺着发愁了。来，这个上釉的盘子给你，比素陶结实，烧了两遍，不会有人一放重了就裂开。这家旅店往后还有多少个冬天，它都能撑得住，而我也打算亲眼见证不少个这样的冬天。

Cloth Scarf: Rough mornings after brew night?
布围巾: 酿酒之夜后早上不好受吧？

Cloth Scarf: The pot's been quiet lately.
布围巾: 锅子最近挺冷清的。

Cloth Scarf: Any brew night planned?
布围巾: 有安排酿酒之夜吗？

Cloth Scarf: What's for the top shelf?
布围巾: 那最好的一层架子上要放什么？

Cloth Scarf: How's the winter pantry?
布围巾: 冬天的储藏怎么样了？

Cloth Scarf: Hand over the dried wild garlic the Inn Keeper asked for.
布围巾: 把旅店老板要的风干野蒜交给他。

Cloth Scarf: Deliver Dried Wild Garlic
布围巾: 递交风干野蒜

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a batch of ale for brew night. The Inn Keeper sniffs the cask, satisfied.
布围巾: 把一批麦酒交给他，供酿酒之夜使用。旅店老板凑近酒桶闻了闻，很满意。

Cloth Scarf: Give Ale
布围巾: 给予麦芽酒

Cloth Scarf: Hand over dried springberries for the winter pantry. The Inn Keeper stacks them with the rest of the stores.
布围巾: 把风干春莓交给他，充实冬天的储藏。旅店老板把它们和其他存货一起码放好。

Cloth Scarf: Give Dried Springberries
布围巾: 给予风干春莓

Cloth Scarf: Hand over milled flour for baking day. The Inn Keeper dusts a hand through it, testing the grind.
布围巾: 把磨好的面粉交给他，供烤面包日使用。旅店老板用手拂过面粉，试试磨得细不细。

Cloth Scarf: Give Flour
布围巾: 给予面粉

Cloth Scarf: Hand over herb paste for the morning-after remedy. The Inn Keeper tucks it behind the bar with a knowing look.
布围巾: 把草药膏交给他，用作宿醉的良方。旅店老板心领神会地把它收到吧台后面。

Cloth Scarf: Give Herb Paste
布围巾: 给予草药糊

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a pot of hot cooked stew. The Inn Keeper ladles out a bowl for herself before it even reaches the counter.
布围巾: 把一锅热腾腾的炖菜交给他。还没等端到柜台上，旅店老板已经先给自己盛了一碗。

Cloth Scarf: Give Hot Stew
布围巾: 给予热炖菜

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a bottle for the top shelf. The Inn Keeper holds it up to the firelight, admiring the color.
布围巾: 把一瓶酒交给他，放到最好的架子上。旅店老板举着瓶子对着炉火，欣赏着酒的颜色。

Cloth Scarf: Give Wine
布围巾: 给予葡萄酒

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some leather.
布围巾: 我会给你带皮革来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Truth be told, the belts on the grindstone are worn thin as paper. Bring me some hides, small leather will do fine, and I can patch them up proper instead of praying every morning.
布围巾: 说实话，磨石上的传动带都磨得跟纸一样薄了。给我带点兽皮来，小块皮革就够用，我好好补一补，省得每天早上都得祈祷它别断。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some planks.
布围巾: 我会给你带木板来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: One more thing, since you're clearly the helpful sort. My workbench is missing a good few planks, don't suppose you've got any spare from that sawmill of yours?
布围巾: 还有一件事，看你这么乐于助人。我的工作台还缺不少木板，你那边的锯木厂该不会正好有多余的吧？

Cloth Scarf: Glad it helped.
布围巾: 很高兴能帮上忙。

Cloth Scarf: Now that's a proper patch job. Stones'll turn smooth as a millpond now. Here, I've been meaning to put up a hunter's platform out past the fields, figured you'd want the plans more than I would.
布围巾: 这补得像样。磨石现在转得跟磨坊池塘一样顺滑了。来，我一直想在田地那边搭个猎人平台，寻思着这图纸对你比对我更有用。

Cloth Scarf: Happy to help.
布围巾: 很乐意帮忙。

Cloth Scarf: Perfect, just what the bench needed. You've a good eye for craft, you know. Here's something for the trouble, an old stonecutting trick my father showed me. Might come in handy for flooring.
布围巾: 正好，工作台就缺这个。你手艺上的眼光是真不错。这个给你，作为谢礼——是我父亲教我的一个老石匠诀窍，铺地板的时候说不定用得上。

Cloth Scarf: Need anything for the mill?
布围巾: 磨坊有什么需要的吗？

Cloth Scarf: Anything else you're short on?
布围巾: 还缺什么别的东西吗？

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a small piece of leather for the Miller's grindstone belts. He turns it over, testing the give in it, and nods.
布围巾: 把一小块皮革交给磨坊主，用于修补传动带。他把皮革翻来覆去，试了试韧性，点了点头。

Cloth Scarf: Give Small Leather
布围巾: 给予小块皮革

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a stack of planks for the Miller's workbench. He sets them against the wall, already planning what to build.
布围巾: 把一摞木板交给磨坊主，用于修理工作台。他把木板靠墙放好，已经开始盘算要做什么了。

Cloth Scarf: Give Planks
布围巾: 给予木板

Cloth Scarf: I'll see if she has one to spare.
布围巾: 我去看看她能不能匀出一件来。

Cloth Scarf: Winter fieldwork is a misery without the right coat, and I hear the Weaver's cut a fine one lately. If you could bring me one of her cloth coats, I'd finally survey properly instead of shivering through it.
布围巾: 没有一件合适的外套，冬季的田野考察简直是种折磨，我听说织工最近裁了几件不错的。你要是能给我带一件她做的布外套来，我总算能好好做实地考察，而不是一路冻得发抖了。

Cloth Scarf: I'll pass that along, Professor.
布围巾: 我会带话给她的，教授。

Cloth Scarf: Warm as promised, good stitching too. Tell the Weaver a scholar's gratitude keeps him from freezing in a ditch this winter. Here, a vest pattern, quilted the same way, in case you ever need one yourself.
布围巾: 果然如说的那样暖和，针脚也很好。跟织工说一声，一位学者的感激，会让他今年冬天不至于冻死在沟渠里。来，这个背心花样给你，同样是绗缝的，说不定哪天你自己也用得上。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some clay.
布围巾: 我会给您带黏土来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Ah, yes! A ruin out past the old tree line, I surveyed it years ago, half-collapsed even then. I've always meant to reconstruct it in miniature. Bring me clay and I'll finally have the material to try.
布围巾: 啊，对了！林线外有一处废墟，我多年前勘察过，那时就已经半塌了。我一直想把它复原成一座微缩模型。给我带些黏土来，我总算有材料可以试试了。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some metal nuggets.
布围巾: 我会给您带金属块来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: There's an old legend the villagers used to tell, a dragon in the hills, more metaphor than beast, I suspect, but a fine subject for a cast figure all the same. Bring me some metal nuggets and I'll see what I can make of it.
布围巾: 村民们过去常讲一个古老的传说，说山里有条巨龙，我估计与其说是野兽，不如说是个比喻，不过用来铸一尊塑像，倒是个不错的题材。给我带些金属块来，我看看能做出什么。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you bones or antler.
布围巾: 我会给您带骨头或鹿角来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: One more project, if you'll indulge me. I've been reconstructing an old armor style from bone and antler, lamellar work, older than anything smithed. Bring me bones or antler and I'll show you how it was done.
布围巾: 再容我提一个项目。我一直在复原一种用骨头和鹿角制成的古老铠甲样式，是札甲工艺，比任何锻造的东西都要古老。给我带骨头或鹿角来，我教你这门手艺是怎么做的。

Cloth Scarf: Happy to humor you, Professor.
布围巾: 很乐意奉陪，教授。

Cloth Scarf: Marvelous, good workable clay, no grit or shale in it at all. I've spent the evening sketching the castle from memory, towers and all, and I think I've finally got the proportions of that collapsed east wall right after eleven years of guessing. Here, the figurine pattern is yours. It's the least I can offer for humoring an old scholar's nostalgia, and honestly the least of what you've earned for it.
布围巾: 太好了，这黏土很好用，没有一点砂砾或页岩碎屑。我花了一整晚，凭记忆勾勒出那座城堡的样子，连塔楼都画出来了，我想我终于把那面倒塌的东墙的比例弄对了，猜了整整十一年。来，这个塑像花样归你了。这是我为一个老学者的怀旧之情能做的最起码的回报，说实话，这也远不及你应得的。

Cloth Scarf: A fine lesson, Professor.
布围巾: 上了很好的一课，教授。

Cloth Scarf: Good weight to these, enough to cast properly without the metal thinning out mid-pour. Here's the dragon figurine pattern, legend cast in clay and metal same as the old villagers must have imagined it, more shape than scale, more shadow than beast. Might teach the village children a thing or two about where stories come from, and maybe teach the rest of us that a good tale doesn't need to be true to be worth keeping.
布围巾: 这些分量正好，够用来好好浇铸，不至于中途金属变薄。给，这是龙形塑像的花样，用黏土和金属浇铸出的传说，就跟当年村民们想象的一样，与其说是鳞片，不如说是轮廓，与其说是野兽，不如说是影子。也许能让村里的孩子们学到点故事从何而来的道理，也许还能让我们这些大人明白，一个好故事，不必是真的，也值得被留存下来。

Cloth Scarf: I'll wear it with pride, Professor.
布围巾: 我会骄傲地穿着它的，教授。

Cloth Scarf: Exactly the material I needed, clean and dry, no rot in it to weaken the lacing. Here's the reconstruction, bone lamellar, laced the old way, plate over plate the way it was worn generations before anyone in this valley learned to smelt. Wear it and you're carrying a piece of scholarship as much as armor, and one fewer forgotten technique in the world besides.
布围巾: 正是我需要的材料，干净又干燥，没有一点腐朽会削弱绳结的强度。这是复原之作，骨制札甲，用古法穿系，一片压一片，正是这山谷里的人学会冶炼之前好几代人穿戴的方式。穿上它，你携带的不只是一件铠甲，更是一份学问，这世上也因此少了一门被遗忘的技艺。

Cloth Scarf: Anything you need for the field?
布围巾: 田野考察需要什么吗？

Cloth Scarf: You mentioned a ruin once?
布围巾: 您以前提过一处废墟？

Cloth Scarf: Something cast from legend?
布围巾: 用传说来铸点什么？

Cloth Scarf: You mentioned historical armor?
布围巾: 您提过历史上的铠甲？

Cloth Scarf: Hand over bones or antler for the Professor's armor reconstruction. He lays the piece out on the table, comparing it to a sketch.
布围巾: 把骨头或鹿角交给教授，用于他的铠甲复原工作。他把材料摆在桌上，对照着草图仔细比对。

Cloth Scarf: Give Bones or Antler
布围巾: 给予骨头或鹿角

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a lump of clay for the Professor's ruined castle. He turns it over, already sketching towers in his mind.
布围巾: 把一块黏土交给教授，用于他的废墟城堡模型。他把黏土翻来覆去地看，脑海里已经开始勾勒塔楼的模样。

Cloth Scarf: Give Clay
布围巾: 给予粘土

Cloth Scarf: Hand over a cloth coat for winter fieldwork. He shrugs it on immediately, testing the warmth.
布围巾: 把一件布外套交给教授，用于冬季田野考察。他立刻披上试了试保暖效果。

Cloth Scarf: Give Cloth Coat
布围巾: 给予布外套

Cloth Scarf: Hand over metal nuggets for the Professor's dragon cast. He weighs them in his palm, pleased at the heft.
布围巾: 把金属块交给教授，用于他的龙形塑像铸造。他在掌心掂了掂分量，很满意。

Cloth Scarf: Give Metal Nuggets
布围巾: 给予金属块

Cloth Scarf: I'll see what she's pressing.
布围巾: 我去看看她在压榨什么。

Cloth Scarf: I heard the Apothecary's finally pressing pigment worth using. If you can get me two batches, different shades, I've got a pattern that wants three colors instead of one. Worth the extra trip, I promise you.
布围巾: 我听说药剂师终于压出了能用的颜料。你要是能给我弄来两批，不同色调的，我这儿有个花样正好要用三种颜色，不是一种。多跑这一趟绝对值，我向你保证。

Cloth Scarf: I'll pass that along.
布围巾: 我会带话给她的。

Cloth Scarf: Three colors, just like that. The Apothecary always did have a good eye for a shade, better than mine, if I'm honest. Here, the tricolor pattern's yours, tell her I said her powders made it possible.
布围巾: 三种颜色，说到就到。药剂师挑色调的眼光一直很好，说实话，比我还强。来，这个三色花样给你，告诉她一声，是她的粉末让这一切成为可能的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some cloth.
布围巾: 我会给你带布料来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Since you asked, bring me a length of cloth you've made yourself, off your own loom or someone else's, I don't mind. I want to see what hands other than mine can do with warp and weft.
布围巾: 你既然问了，那就给我带一段你自己织的布来，用你自己的织机还是别人的都无所谓。我想看看除了我这双手之外，别人是怎么摆弄经纬线的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you a scarf.
布围巾: 我会给你带一条围巾来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Bring me a cloth scarf, one you've sewn, not one you've bought off some peddler. I want to see if you've been paying attention to how I put a seam together.
布围巾: 给我带一条布围巾来，得是你自己缝的，不是从哪个货郎那儿买来的。我想看看你有没有留意过我是怎么把针脚缝在一起的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you a bundle.
布围巾: 我会给你带一捆来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Winter's coming and my own fiber stores are thin. Bring me a bundle of wool or fiber and I'll show you something to wear under everything else, warmest trick I know.
布围巾: 冬天要来了，我自己的纤维存货不多了。给我带一捆羊毛或纤维来，我教你个贴身穿的窍门，是我知道的最暖和的一招。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you a large cloth.
布围巾: 我会给你带一大块布来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: I've had my eye on a full coat pattern, but it wants a large piece of cloth to work with, more than a scarf, more than a shirt. Bring me one and I'll cut it for you myself.
布围巾: 我一直惦记着一件长外套的花样，可它要用的布得是一大块，比围巾多，比衬衫也多。给我带一块来，我亲自给你裁。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some large leather.
布围巾: 我会给你带一大块皮革来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: Leather's not my usual trade, but I know what to do with a large piece of it. Bring me one and I'll cut you an apron, the kind that saves your clothes from every spark and spill.
布围巾: 皮革不是我平常干的活，不过一大块皮革，我知道该怎么处理。给我带一块来，我给你裁条围裙，能护住你的衣服，不管是火星子还是洒出来的东西。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you some leather.
布围巾: 我会给你带皮革来的。

Cloth Scarf: Maybe another time.
布围巾: 改天再说吧。

Cloth Scarf: One more, and then I'll leave your errands be for a while. Bring me a small piece of leather and I'll show you how to make sandals that won't fall apart the first time you cross a river.
布围巾: 再来最后一件，之后我会让你的差事清静一阵子。给我带一小块皮革来，我教你怎么做一双凉鞋，过一次河都散不了架的那种。

Cloth Scarf: Glad it's useful.
布围巾: 很高兴能派上用场。

Cloth Scarf: Now that's honest work, even weave, tight edges. You've got the hands for this, whether you know it or not. Here, I sketched a wall hanging pattern that wants exactly this kind of cloth. It's yours.
布围巾: 这才叫实在的手艺，织得均匀，边缘也紧实。你这双手是吃这碗饭的料，不管你自己知不知道。来，我画了个壁挂花样，正好要用这种布。这个给你了。

Cloth Scarf: It's a fine pattern.
布围巾: 这花样真不错。

Cloth Scarf: Look at that seam, hardly a pucker in it. You have been paying attention. Here, a hood-and-cape pattern I've been saving, a chaperon, sturdy enough for real work and sharp enough for the village square.
布围巾: 瞧瞧这针脚，几乎看不出一点皱褶。看来你是真留意过。给，一个连帽披风的花样，我一直留着的，一件兜帽披风，结实得能干正经活，样子也精神得能穿去村广场。

Cloth Scarf: I'll be glad of them come winter.
布围巾: 等冬天来了我会很感激有它们的。

Cloth Scarf: Plenty here for a proper undergarment. Long johns, snug at the ankle and the wrist, keep the wind from ever finding skin. My mother swore by them and so will you.
布围巾: 这些够做一件像样的内衣了。长内裤，脚踝和手腕都贴身，风别想找到一点皮肤的缝隙。我母亲一直对这个赞不绝口，你穿了也会一样。

Cloth Scarf: I'll wear it proudly.
布围巾: 我会骄傲地穿着它。

Cloth Scarf: That's plenty of cloth, good weight to it too. Here's the coat pattern, full-length, warm as a hearth. Wear it well.
布围巾: 这布够多了，分量也够。给，长外套的花样，一直到脚踝那么长，暖和得跟炉火似的。好好穿着它。

Cloth Scarf: That'll save my clothes.
布围巾: 这能保护好我的衣服了。

Cloth Scarf: Good hide, thick enough to matter. Here's the apron pattern, worth its weight the first time a spark jumps off a fire and lands somewhere you'd rather it hadn't.
布围巾: 好皮子，够厚实。给，围裙的花样，等哪天火星子蹦出来落在你不想让它落的地方，你就知道这东西有多值了。

Cloth Scarf: You've kept me busy, and I'm grateful for it.
布围巾: 你可让我忙活了不少，不过我很感激。

Cloth Scarf: Small piece, but the right size for a good sole. Here's the sandal pattern, laced tight, won't slip off in the mud or the shallows. That's the last errand I've got for now, and I mean it this time.
布围巾: 一小块，正好够做一副好鞋底。给，凉鞋的花样，系带紧实，泥地里、浅滩里都不会松脱。这是我目前最后一件差事了，这次是真的。

Cloth Scarf: Homestead
布围巾: 安家

Cloth Scarf: You've come prepared to settle down. Start with a cabin kit, two rain cistern kits, and a stockpile of building materials (30 planks, 30 mud bricks, 30 heavy stones, 50 stones, 10 logs, 50 copper nails, 10 rope). Carry the kits with you and use Place to raise them wherever you want to build your homestead — each kit can only be placed once.
布围巾: 你有备而来，准备就此安家落户。开局携带一个小屋套件、两个集雨桶套件，以及一批建筑材料储备（30块木板、30块泥砖、30块重石、50块石头、10根原木、50根铜钉、10段绳子）。随身携带这些套件，想在哪里建立家园就使用「放置」在那里搭建——每个套件只能放置一次。

Cloth Scarf: Architecture, passed with a design I'll admit I stole a diagram from for next term's lecture. Water doesn't forgive a bad angle the way earth does, but you found the right one. A water-driven sawmill and grinding mill are within your skill now, real ones, not the toy models I sketch on the board. Combine it with a Metallurgy degree and you'll be casting your own forge fittings before the season turns.
布围巾: 建筑学，通过了，我得承认，你的设计图我打算偷去用在下学期的讲课里。水流可不像土地那样，会原谅一个糟糕的角度，可你找对了那个角度。如今水力锯木厂和水力磨坊都在你的能力范围之内了，是真正的实物，不是我在黑板上画的那种玩具模型。再拿下一个冶金学学位，用不了一季，你就能自己铸造锻炉配件了。

Cloth Scarf: Armorer, passed, and passed properly, no student of mine gets a breastplate pattern without proving they understand why the rivets go where they go. Copper will do in a pinch, but iron will actually keep you alive out past the tree line, helm, greaves, gauntlets, the full set is yours to make now. I'd rather you never need it. I'd rather you have it anyway.
布围巾: 制甲，通过了，而且是货真价实地通过。我的学生想拿到胸甲的花样，就必须先证明自己明白铆钉为什么要钉在那些位置上。铜制的凑合一下还行，可真正能在林线之外保住你性命的是铁——头盔、护胫、护手，整套装备现在都在你的制作能力范围之内了。我宁愿你永远用不上它。我也宁愿你无论如何都拥有它。

Cloth Scarf: You passed Fishing, and unlike most of my courses this one I actually enjoy grading, mostly because it involves an afternoon by the water instead of a stack of essays. The iron fittings for a proper rod are yours to build now, sturdier than anything whittled from green wood. My uncle's mythical river monster is still out there uncaught, incidentally, should you fancy a rematch on his behalf.
布围巾: 你通过了钓鱼课，跟我大多数课程不同，这门课的评分我是真心喜欢，主要是因为它意味着在水边度过一个下午，而不是批改一摞论文。如今你已经能制作一副像样鱼竿所需的铁制配件了，比任何用生木削出来的都结实。顺带一提，我叔叔那条传说中的河怪至今还没被钓上来过，你要是愿意替他打一场复仇之战，我不反对。

Cloth Scarf: Herbalism, passed! That's the course I'm proudest to teach, truth be told, plants don't lecture back and neither do the students who love them. You've earned the plans for a proper apothecary's cabin now, and the knowledge to mix a real healing draught rather than just crushing leaves and hoping. Go build something with it. The forest's given you enough of itself; it's time you gave a little back.
布围巾: 药草学，通过了！说实话，这是我最引以为豪的一门课，植物不会顶嘴，喜爱植物的学生也一样不会。你如今已经赢得了一座像样的药剂师小屋的图纸，还有调配真正治疗药水的知识，而不再只是捣碎叶子碰运气了。拿它去建造点什么吧。这片森林已经给了你足够多的馈赠，是时候回馈一点了。

Cloth Scarf: Medicine, of all courses, is the one I can't fully teach from a lectern, and you passed it anyway. Most of it is watching someone shiver through a fever and knowing which of your remedies actually helps and which just makes you feel useful. You'll carry that instinct with you now whether you're tending yourself or anyone fool enough to get hurt near you. Don't let it go quiet from disuse.
布围巾: 医学，在所有课程里，是我最没法单靠讲台教全的一门，可你还是通过了。这门学问，大半在于看着一个人在高烧中颤抖，还要分辨出你手头的疗法哪个真正管用，哪个不过是让你自己感觉有用而已。从今往后，不论是照顾自己，还是照顾哪个傻乎乎在你身边受了伤的人，你都会带着这份直觉。别让它因为闲置而生疏。

Cloth Scarf: Passed, and properly, not a squeak of luck in it. Metallurgy is the course that weeds out the impatient, half my students give up the moment the ore refuses to cooperate. You didn't. Sheet metal will behave itself for you from here on, worked thin and even instead of cracking under the hammer, and I expect you already have a project or two in mind for it.
布围巾: 通过了，而且是扎扎实实地通过，没有半点运气的成分。冶金学专挑没耐心的人淘汰，我一半的学生一旦矿石不听话，立刻就打退堂鼓了。你没有。从今往后，薄板金属在你手里会乖乖听话，锤打出来薄而均匀，不会开裂，我料想你心里已经有一两个用得上它的计划了。

I taught that woman her Herbalism same as I'm teaching you, and now she's the one mixing draughts instead of me lecturing about them. There's a particular satisfaction in watching a student outgrow the lectern entirely. Do visit her stall if you haven't; between the two of us this village is dangerously well medicated.
布围巾: 这么说你已经听说了，药剂师的小屋已经建成。药草学是我教给她的，就跟我现在教你一样，如今调制药剂的人成了她，不再是我站在讲台上空谈了。看着一个学生彻底超越讲台，自有一种特别的满足感。要是你还没去过她的摊位，一定要去看看；有我们俩在，这村子的医药供应，简直富余得有点过头了。

Cloth Scarf: The Village Hall, up at last. I stopped by to see it and found myself lecturing the notice board out of old habit before I caught myself. It's a strange thing, watching a settlement decide it's permanent enough to need a civic building. Ten years ago this was a clearing with a fire pit and my own stubborn refusal to leave. Now it has a Hall. Write that down somewhere, it's the sort of thing histories forget to mention.
布围巾: 村公所，总算立起来了。我过去瞧了一眼，结果不知不觉，出于老习惯，竟对着告示板讲起课来，才猛然回过神。看着一处聚落认定自己已经足够长久，需要一座公共建筑，这感觉挺奇妙的。十年前这里不过是一片空地，一个火坑，还有我固执地拒绝离开。如今它有了一座公所。把这个记下来吧，这正是史书容易遗漏的那类事情。

Cloth Scarf: Wonderful, truly. I've had that ruin's floor plan sketched on the same scrap of parchment for eleven years now, waiting on someone patient enough to indulge me. Don't rush the clay-gathering on my account, but I'll admit I'll be watching the door a little more eagerly than usual until you're back.
布围巾: 太好了，真的太好了。那处废墟的平面图，我在同一张羊皮纸残片上画了整整十一年，一直在等一个有耐心陪我这么折腾的人。不必因为我而急着去收集黏土，不过我承认，在你回来之前，我望向门口的次数，怕是会比平常多一些。

Cloth Scarf: Good, good. Every village needs a monster in its hills, it gives the children something to be brave about and the adults something to blame the weather on. Whether the dragon was ever real hardly matters to the casting, metal doesn't care for the difference between history and a good story anyway.
布围巾: 好，很好。每个村子的山里都该有个怪物，这样孩子们才有勇气可以展示，大人们也有个东西可以怪罪坏天气。那条龙究竟是不是真的存在，对铸造这件事来说其实无关紧要，反正金属才不在乎历史和好故事之间的区别呢。

Cloth Scarf: Excellent. Most smiths won't touch bone work, too slow, not enough profit in it, but there's a reason it kept people alive for longer than metal's been common in these hills. I want to see the technique survive somewhere other than my own notes before I'm too old to demonstrate the lacing myself.
布围巾: 太好了。大多数铁匠不愿碰骨制品，太费工夫，又没什么利润，可它能在金属在这片山地普及之前，保住人们的性命这么久，自有它的道理。我希望在自己老得连穿系的手法都演示不了之前，能看到这门技艺不只留存在我的笔记里。

Cloth Scarf: We've got ourselves a Village Hall now, notice board and all. Half the village crowded round it the first morning just to watch the paint dry, myself included, I'll admit. My father used to say a settlement isn't really a village until it has somewhere to argue about its own business out loud instead of over ale at my bar. Suppose that makes us official now.
布围巾: 我们现在有村公所了，连告示板都有。开张头一天早上，半个村子的人都挤在那儿看油漆晾干，我自己也在里头，不瞒你说。我父亲以前常说，一个聚落要是没个能大声吵自家事的地方，光在我吧台喝着酒争论，那就算不上真正的村子。我看这下咱们算是名正言顺了。

Cloth Scarf: Your bar's argument monopoly is over, then.
布围巾: 这么说，你吧台的“吵架垄断权”要没了。

Cloth Scarf: Did you hear? The miller's got a proper roof over his head at last, instead of sleeping next to that wheel of his like it might wander off in the night. Known the man twenty years and I don't think I've ever seen him build anything for himself before, always some neighbor's fence or someone else's barn first. Glad to see him finally spend the effort on his own walls.
布围巾: 你听说了吗？磨坊主总算有了像样的屋顶，不用再睡在水车旁边，好像怕它半夜自己跑了似的。我认识这人二十年了，印象里他从没为自己盖过什么，总是先给邻居修篱笆，先给别人盖谷仓。看到他终于肯为自己的墙费点力气，我很高兴。

Cloth Scarf: Well earned, from what I hear of him.
布围巾: 听你这么一说，这是他应得的。

Cloth Scarf: The stall's turning a real profit these days, and everyone from the miller to the market vendor keeps telling me it's because word finally got around about this place. Every cottage, every well bucket, every fool commission the Professor's students dragged back from the hills, it all adds up to something. I didn't think I'd live to see this valley become a place worth writing home about, but here we are. Drinks are on the house tonight, don't argue with me about it.
布围巾: 摊位这些日子真赚了钱，从磨坊主到市场摊贩，个个都跟我说，这是因为这地方的名声终于传出去了。每一座小屋，每一只水井吊桶，教授学生们从山里带回来的每一件傻乎乎的委托，全都累积成了点什么。我没想到自己能活着看到这山谷变成一个值得写信回家提起的地方，可现在我们做到了。今晚喝的都算我的，别跟我争。

Cloth Scarf: I certainly won't argue with free drinks.
布围巾: 免费的酒，我可不会跟你争。

Cloth Scarf: Somewhere along the way this stopped feeling like a handful of buildings and started feeling like a village people actually talk about. Travelers passing through ask after us by name now, instead of just squinting at the map wondering if there's anything worth the detour. Halfway to somewhere, I'd say, and I mean to see the rest of it built before I'm too old to pour the celebration ale myself.
布围巾: 不知道从什么时候起，这地方不再只是几栋房子的堆砌，开始变成了一个人们真正会提起的村子。路过的旅人现在会直接打听我们的名字，而不是盯着地图眯眼琢磨绕这个道值不值得。我看这算是走到半路了，我打算亲眼看着剩下的部分建起来，趁我还没老到倒不动庆功酒。

Cloth Scarf: You've built something worth talking about.
布围巾: 你们建起了一个值得被人提起的地方。

Cloth Scarf: The weaver's cottage went up too, did you see it on your way in? She hung a length of her own cloth over the doorway for a curtain before the paint had even dried, couldn't wait a single day to make the place hers. Between her and the miller both settling proper, this village is starting to look less like a rest stop and more like somewhere people actually mean to stay.
布围巾: 织工的小屋也盖起来了，你进来的时候看见了吗？油漆都还没干，她就已经挂上自己织的一匹布当门帘了，一天都等不了，非要马上把这地方变成自己的。有她和磨坊主都正经安顿下来，这村子越来越不像个歇脚的地方了，倒像是个人们真心打算长住的地方。

Cloth Scarf: It's coming together nicely.
布围巾: 这一切都渐渐成形了，真不错。

Cloth Scarf: Bless you, truly. A man can only eat the same thin broth so many nights running before he starts dreaming about it. Take your time, mind, I'd rather wait a week for a proper stew than eat a rushed one tonight.
布围巾: 太谢谢你了，真的。一个人连着喝那么多晚一样的稀汤，做梦都会梦见它。慢慢来没关系，比起今晚吃一锅赶出来的炖菜，我宁愿多等一星期吃到一锅像样的。

Cloth Scarf: I'll bring you the best I've got.
布围巾: 我会把我能做出的最好的带给你。

Cloth Scarf: Good, good, brew night without proper ale is just a room full of disappointed regulars, and I'd rather not test how disappointed they can get. Bring it when you're ready, no rush, though if you happen to pass by on a brew night itself I won't turn away an early delivery.
布围巾: 好，好，酿酒之夜没有像样的麦酒，那就只是一屋子失望的常客，我可不想试探他们到底能失望到什么地步。你准备好了再带来，不急，不过要是正好赶上酿酒之夜路过，提前送到我也不会拒绝。

Cloth Scarf: I'll have it here in time.
布围巾: 我会及时送到的。

Cloth Scarf: Now you're talking. I've been saving the good glassware for exactly this occasion, dust and all, and it's high time I had something worth pouring into it. Don't skimp on the quality, either, my regulars have opinions and they are not shy about sharing them.
布围巾: 这话我爱听。我一直留着那套好玻璃器皿，就等着这样的场合，连灰都没舍得擦，现在总算有值得倒进去的东西了。质量可别打折扣，我那些常客都有自己的看法，而且从不吝于说出来。

Cloth Scarf: Only the good stuff, I promise.
布围巾: 我保证只带最好的东西来。

Cloth Scarf: Much obliged. Winter's got a way of catching everyone off guard even when we all know it's coming, same as it does every single year. My mother used to say a full pantry in autumn is worth more than gold come the deep frost, and she was rarely wrong about that sort of thing.
布围巾: 太感激了。冬天总有本事让每个人都措手不及，明明大家都知道它要来，年年如此。我母亲以前常说，秋天存满的储藏柜，比等到严寒时的金子还金贵，这种事她很少说错。

Cloth Scarf: I'll make sure the pantry's stocked.
布围巾: 我会确保储藏柜是满的。

Cloth Scarf: Thorne and Corrin hold the square by day, Vane takes the night. We rotate the jail step between the four of us so it's never left unwatched. Quiet work, mostly -- and I intend to keep it that way.
布围巾: 索恩和科林白天守着广场，瓦恩负责夜班。我们四人轮流站监狱的岗，确保那里从不无人看守。大多时候都是些平静的差事——我也打算让它继续平静下去。

Cloth Scarf: A word, before we go any further. I've heard what's been said about you, and I'll not pretend I haven't. I'm not hauling you in over it -- not yet. But hear this once, because I won't say it twice: keep on, and the Watch stops giving you the benefit of the doubt. Keep on past that, and you're not welcome inside these walls at all. Mind yourself.
布围巾: 在我们继续之前，容我说一句。关于你的传言我都听说了，不会假装没这回事。我暂时不会把你抓起来——现在还不会。但这话我只说一次，听清楚了：再这样下去，巡逻队就不会再对你网开一面。再往下走，你在这城墙之内就不再受欢迎了。自己小心点。

Cloth Scarf: Understood, Captain.
布围巾: 明白了，队长。

布围巾: 隐藏追踪器：记录铜制箱子警觉计数器上次写入的季节。

Cloth Scarf: Captain Reeve Sterling moves to block your way, sword still in its scabbard.
布围巾: 里夫·斯特林队长上前拦住你的去路，佩剑仍在鞘中。

Cloth Scarf: He gets a hand on you and turns you back. He does not draw.
布围巾: 他一把抓住你，将你推了回去。他始终没有拔剑。

Cloth Scarf: You slip past his reach before he can close his grip.
布围巾: 你在他收拢手掌之前从他臂展下溜了过去。

Cloth Scarf: The captain presses forward, open-handed, herding you away from the square.
布围巾: 队长空着双手向前逼近，把你从广场驱赶开去。

Cloth Scarf: He crowds you back a step and holds you there.
布围巾: 他把你逼退一步，并将你稳稳挡在原地。

Cloth Scarf: You give ground and break the line he was trying to hold.
布围巾: 你后退让步，冲破了他试图守住的防线。

Cloth Scarf: Captain Reeve Sterling stops you.
布围巾: 里夫·斯特林队长拦下了你。

Cloth Scarf: He plants himself in your path with one hand raised and the other well clear of his sword. "Stand down and come with me," he says, "or don't. But think on it first."
布围巾: 他挡在你面前，一手抬起，另一只手远离剑柄。“放下武器，跟我走，”他说，“或者不跟。但先好好想清楚。”

Cloth Scarf: Think better of it
布围巾: 再想想，算了

Cloth Scarf: Attack the captain
布围巾: 攻击队长

Cloth Scarf: The Watch has you surrounded.
布围巾: 巡逻队已将你团团围住。

Cloth Scarf: The captain is not alone this time. The Watch has closed from every side, and there is no gap left to talk your way through. "No more warnings," Sterling says.
布围巾: 这一次队长并非独自前来。巡逻队已从四面合围，再没有留下任何可供你辩解脱身的缝隙。“不会再有警告了。”斯特林说。

Cloth Scarf: Fight your way out
布围巾: 杀出重围

Cloth Scarf: Sterling closes the distance and takes hold of you.
布围巾: 斯特林迅速逼近，一把将你擒住。

Cloth Scarf: You are held fast. It is over, and he never drew the blade.
布围巾: 你被牢牢制住。一切都结束了，而他自始至终没有拔剑。

Cloth Scarf: You wrench free for a heartbeat — and his hand closes on you again.
布围巾: 你挣脱了一瞬——随即他的手又一次扣住了你。

Cloth Scarf: The captain walks you to the jail without another word. You are not hurt. You are simply no longer free.
布围巾: 队长一言不发地把你押往牢房。你毫发无伤，只是从此不再自由。

Cloth Scarf: Captain Sterling is done waiting.
布围巾: 斯特林队长不打算再等下去了。

Cloth Scarf: "I have given you every chance I have to give," the captain says, and this time he does not stop to argue. He takes hold of you and does not let go.
布围巾: “我能给的机会，都已经给过你了。”队长说道，而这一次他没有停下来争辩。他擒住你，再不松手。

Cloth Scarf: Let him take you
布围巾: 束手就擒

布围巾: 已给出的机会

布围巾: 隐藏计数器：你有多少次在与斯特林队长的冲突面前选择了退让。
